title: Diversity-Preserved Distribution Matching Distillation for Fast Visual Synthesis
claim: Assigning different roles to early and late steps of a few-step student preserves diversity while a standard distillation loss refines quality.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, student row below teacher row, detach break
description: A wide training-pipeline diagram with rounded boxes and gray arrows. On the left, a noise image feeds a frozen gray Teacher (K-step inference), which produces a parrot image. That image goes to a red-outlined loss box, ℓ_Div. Below, a blue Student (1-step inference) produces a blurry first-step prediction that also feeds ℓ_Div. A red 'Detaching' label with a slash marks a break in the arrow to a second Student (N−1 steps). That student's output x_θ feeds the ℓ_FM box, which receives an auxiliary prediction from a shaded 'Auxiliary model training' panel. The noisy z_t goes to a frozen Teacher and an Auxiliary model (peach). Their scores, s_tea and s_stu, meet at ℓ_DMD on the right. Flame and snowflake icons mark trainable and frozen modules.
caption: Training pipeline of DP-DMD. The student’s first denoising step is supervised by a teacher-derived intermediate state through the target-prediction loss ℓDiv. Gradients are detached after this step to prevent the DMD loss from overriding the early diversity signal. The remaining N −1 steps are trained with the standard DMD loss, where teacher and auxiliary model scores provide distribution-matching guidance for perceptual quality refinement. This role-separated design preserves sample diversity while maintaining high-quality few-step generation.
abstract: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) facilitates few-step image generation by aligning a distilled student with a reference multi-step teacher. In practice, however, optimizing DMD can reduce sample diversity in few-step synthesis, and existing remedies typically rely on perceptual or adversarial regularization, leading to stability and scalability challenges during training. Here, we describe diversity-preserved DMD (DP-DMD), a role-separated distillation method inspired by the complementary roles of early and late denoising steps. Specifically, the first distillation step is trained with a teacher-derived target-prediction objective (e.g., v-prediction) to preserve sample diversity, while the remaining steps are optimized with the standard DMD loss to refine perceptual quality. DP-DMD, with no perceptual or adversarial regularization, no additional modules, and no teacher-generated reference samples, preserves sample diversity while maintaining competitive visual quality under few-step sampling, providing a simple and stable alternative to other DMD variants.
